Feature Partitioning with MPCurver

Source: vignettes/partition.Rmd
partition.Rmd
library(MPCurver)
set.seed(42)

The feature-partition problem

The single-ordering model assumes that all features share one latent sample ordering. The partition model instead uses a fixed number MM of candidate orderings and a feature-level assignment Zj∈{1,…,M}Z_j \in \{1,\ldots,M\}. If feature jj belongs to ordering mm,

xij∣Zj=m,Ci(m)=k,Uj∼N(ujk,σj2). x_{ij} \mid Z_j=m,\; C_i^{(m)}=k,\; U_j \sim N(u_{jk},\sigma_j^2).

The feature variance σj2\sigma_j^2 is shared across orderings. Each conditional trajectory has an ordering-specific smoothness parameter,

Uj∣Zj=m∼N(0,(λjmQK)−1). U_j \mid Z_j=m \sim N\!\left(0,(\lambda_{jm}Q_K)^{-1}\right).

The public interface uses intrinsic_dim = M. Version 0.3.0 supports fitting a user-specified fixed MM; automatic greedy selection of MM is temporarily unavailable because the fixed-MM variational objective is not itself a complexity-penalized model-selection criterion.

Structural variational family

For every M≥2M \geq 2, MPCurver uses

q(C,Z,U)=∏m=1M∏i=1nq(Ci(m))∏j=1dq(Zj)q(Uj∣Zj). q(C,Z,U) = \prod_{m=1}^M\prod_{i=1}^n q(C_i^{(m)}) \prod_{j=1}^d q(Z_j)q(U_j\mid Z_j).

Write

q(Ci(m)=k)=rimk,q(Zj=m)=wjm, q(C_i^{(m)}=k)=r_{imk},\qquad q(Z_j=m)=w_{jm},

and

q(Uj∣Zj=m)=N(μjm,Vjm). q(U_j\mid Z_j=m)=N(\mu_{jm},V_{jm}).

This dependence is important: the MM Gaussian factors for feature jj are conditional alternatives under ZjZ_j, rather than MM independent potential trajectories that all exist simultaneously.

Conditional trajectory update

Let Nmk=∑irimkN_{mk}=\sum_i r_{imk}. With estimated feature variance,

Ajm=λjmQK+diag(Nmσj2),bjm=(R(m))TX⋅jσj2, A_{jm} = \lambda_{jm}Q_K +\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{N_m}{\sigma_j^2}\right), \qquad b_{jm} = \frac{(R^{(m)})^T X_{\cdot j}}{\sigma_j^2},

and

Vjm=Ajm−1,μjm=Vjmbjm. V_{jm}=A_{jm}^{-1},\qquad \mu_{jm}=V_{jm}b_{jm}.

The feature-assignment probability wjmw_{jm} does not occur in either the precision or the right-hand side. Therefore a small or zero wjmw_{jm} does not drive the conditional posterior back toward a singular intrinsic prior.

If known observation-level variances vijv_{ij} are supplied through S, the likelihood terms become

Ajm=λjmQK+diagk∑irimkvij,bjmk=∑irimkxijvij. A_{jm} = \lambda_{jm}Q_K +\operatorname{diag}_k\sum_i\frac{r_{imk}}{v_{ij}}, \qquad b_{jmk}=\sum_i\frac{r_{imk}x_{ij}}{v_{ij}}.

Ordering responsibilities

The ordering-specific sample responsibilities still average over feature assignments:

logrimk=+logπmk−12∑jwjm(xij−μjmk)2+Vjm,kkσj2. \log r_{imk} \stackrel{+}{=} \log\pi_{mk} -\frac12\sum_j w_{jm} \frac{(x_{ij}-\mu_{jmk})^2+V_{jm,kk}}{\sigma_j^2}.

Thus wjmw_{jm} affects how strongly feature jj informs ordering mm, while it does not change the definition of the conditional trajectory posterior.

Shared feature variance

For estimated noise, define

Ejm=∑i,krimk[(xij−μjmk)2+Vjm,kk]. E_{jm} = \sum_{i,k}r_{imk} \left[(x_{ij}-\mu_{jmk})^2+V_{jm,kk}\right].

The single shared variance update is

σj2=1n∑m=1MwjmEjm. \sigma_j^2 = \frac1n\sum_{m=1}^M w_{jm}E_{jm}.

Consequently, a partition fit exposes one length-dd vector in fit$params$sigma2. When S is known, this field is NULL.

Feature assignment and local ELBO

The feature assignment uses the complete conditional local ELBO, not only the expected likelihood. Let

Gjm=μjmTQKμjm+tr(QKVjm). G_{jm}=\mu_{jm}^TQ_K\mu_{jm}+\operatorname{tr}(Q_KV_{jm}).

For an intrinsic precision with rank rr and generalized determinant |QK|+|Q_K|_+, the local block BjmB_{jm} contains the expected likelihood, the trajectory prior, the optional lambda prior, and the Gaussian entropy:

Bjm=−n2log(2πσj2)−Ejm2σj2+12[r{logλjm−log(2π)}+log|QK|+−λjmGjm]+logp(λjm)+12[Klog(2πe)+log|Vjm|]. \begin{aligned} B_{jm} =\;&-\frac n2\log(2\pi\sigma_j^2) -\frac{E_{jm}}{2\sigma_j^2}\\ &+\frac12\left[ r\{\log\lambda_{jm}-\log(2\pi)\} +\log|Q_K|_+ -\lambda_{jm}G_{jm} \right]\\ &+\log p(\lambda_{jm}) +\frac12\left[K\log(2\pi e)+\log|V_{jm}|\right]. \end{aligned}

At temperature TT,

wjm∝exp{𝔼logωm+BjmT}. w_{jm} \propto \exp\left\{ \frac{\mathbb E\log\omega_m+B_{jm}}{T} \right\}.

At T=1T=1, objective_history records the fixed-MM structural ELBO. Objective values at different annealing temperatures are not directly comparable; only the fixed-TT segment should be checked for coordinate-ascent monotonicity.

Intrinsic prior with ridge = 0

For an intrinsic random-walk prior, QKQ_K is rank deficient. The conditional posterior precision is nevertheless

λjmQK+Djm, \lambda_{jm}Q_K+D_{jm},

where DjmD_{jm} is supplied by the likelihood and does not vanish with wjmw_{jm}. This is the same posterior-identification mechanism used by the single-ordering CAVI fit. The algorithm does not use feature-weight floors, automatic precision jitter, active/inactive orderings, or freeze/drop states.

ridge remains available as an explicit modelling choice. A positive value makes the trajectory prior proper, but it is not required merely to rescue the conditional posterior from a small feature-assignment weight.

With ridge = 0, the trajectory prior normalization uses the rank and generalized determinant of QKQ_K. Accordingly, the recorded value follows the package’s intrinsic or pseudo-ELBO convention; structural VI fixes the posterior singularity caused by the old fractional update, but it does not turn an improper intrinsic prior into a proper marginal likelihood.

Fitting a fixed number of orderings 

sim <- simulate_dual_trajectory(
  n = 500,
  d1 = 10,
  d2 = 10,
  d_noise = 0,
  sigma = 0.05,
  trajectory_family = c("quadratic", "monotone"),
  seed = 1
)

X <- sim$X
truth <- sim$true_assign
fit_partition <- fit_mpcurve(
  X,
  intrinsic_dim = 2,
  method = "PCA",
  K = 50,
  rw_q = 2,
  ridge = 0,
  verbose = FALSE
)

The returned mpcurve object has one canonical structural state:

  • params$sigma2: shared length-dd variance vector, or NULL with known S;
  • gamma: named list of MM responsibility matrices;
  • conditional_posterior: conditional means and covariances for every ordering;
  • lambda_mat: d×Md\times M smoothness matrix;
  • partition$pi_weights: d×Md\times M feature-assignment probabilities;
  • partition$assign: hard labels obtained from the largest probability;
  • objective_history and temperature_history: fitting diagnostics.

fits remains available only as a derived compatibility view for existing read-only code. These child objects are regenerated from the canonical state; they are not independent fitting states and are not used by do_mpcurve().

plot(fit_partition, plot_type = "elbo")

Inspecting the fixed-M structural objective and the ordering-specific pseudotime views. 

plot(fit_partition, dims = 4)

Inspecting the fixed-M structural objective and the ordering-specific pseudotime views.

Plotting structural trajectory means

For a partition fit, plot_type = "mu" reads the canonical conditional posterior directly. With one selected feature, panel mm displays

E[Uj∣Zj=m] E[U_j \mid Z_j=m]

against normalized latent position for every fixed ordering mm. The panel title reports q(Zj=m)q(Z_j=m), which helps distinguish a well-supported conditional trajectory from a low-probability alternative. The trajectory itself is not multiplied by this assignment probability: it is the mean of the conditional Gaussian branch.

plot(fit_partition, plot_type = "mu", dims = 4)

Conditional posterior mean trajectory for feature 4 under each of the two fixed orderings.

When dims contains two features, each panel instead plots the two conditional mean coordinates against one another along the latent grid. This is useful for comparing the geometric paths implied by the same pair of features under the different ordering assignments.

plot(fit_partition, plot_type = "mu", dims = c(4, 14))

Two-dimensional conditional posterior mean paths for features 4 and 14 under each fixed ordering.

Both forms use conditional_posterior$mean, not an independently updated child fit. Consequently, the displayed paths are exactly the q(Uj∣Zj=m)q(U_j\mid Z_j=m) means used by the structural coordinate updates.

Inspecting the fixed-temperature objective 

t1 <- fit_partition$temperature_history == 1
delta_t1 <- diff(fit_partition$objective_history[t1])
cat("Largest T=1 decrease:", min(c(0, delta_t1)), "\n")
#> Largest T=1 decrease: 0

Partition accuracy 

pred <- as.character(fit_partition$partition$assign)
truth <- as.character(truth)
accuracy <- max(mean(pred == truth), mean(pred != truth))
cat("Partition accuracy:", round(accuracy, 4), "\n")
#> Partition accuracy: 1

Continuing a fit 

fit_partition <- do_mpcurve(fit_partition, iter = 10)

Continuation uses only the canonical structural state and appends exact T=1T=1 coordinate sweeps to objective_history.

Initialization

The default partition_init = "similarity" clusters features and initializes one ordering per feature block. Alternatively, partition_init = "ordering_methods" accepts one method per ordering:

fit3 <- fit_mpcurve(
  X,
  intrinsic_dim = 3,
  partition_init = "ordering_methods",
  method = c("fiedler", "PCA", "PCA"),
  K = 16
)

For estimated noise, sigma2_init is a scalar or length-dd shared variance vector. lambda initializes all entries of lambda_mat; use fix_lambda = TRUE to keep them fixed. sigma2_init cannot be combined with known measurement standard deviations S.

Deprecated transition arguments

The former augmented algorithm exposed freeze_unused_ordering, freeze_feature, their thresholds, and drop_unused_ordering. They are no longer part of the fitting algorithm. During the 0.3.x transition they remain accepted by fit_mpcurve() and do_mpcurve() only to issue a deprecation warning; their values are ignored and new objects do not store active, frozen, effective-weight, or dropped-ordering state.

Practical guidance

  • Choose a fixed, scientifically plausible intrinsic_dim and compare the resulting partitions through stability or external validation.
  • Do not use the raw structural ELBO alone to select MM: with an adaptive ordering prior, an extra nearly empty ordering is not automatically charged a model-complexity penalty.
  • ridge = 0 is the default intrinsic-prior path. Use positive ridge only when a properized trajectory prior is part of the intended model.
  • Inspect only fixed-TT segments for monotonicity.
  • Use multiple initializations when trajectories are non-monotone or weakly separated.

Summary

  • All fixed M≥2M\ge2 fits use structural VI, q(C)q(Z)q(U∣Z)q(C)q(Z)q(U\mid Z).
  • Conditional trajectory precision is independent of wjmw_{jm}.
  • Estimated σj2\sigma_j^2 is shared across orderings.
  • New fits have one canonical state; $fits is a derived compatibility view.
  • Freeze/drop machinery is retired, and greedy cross-MM selection is temporarily unavailable.
